title: Kairo Knox Episode 013 — Three Words. A $359 AI Recommendation
intended_viewer: Everyday online shoppers who want accurate, entertaining and useful explanations of AI decision systems
audience_benefit: See how injected personal context can change a simulated AI recommendation; learn to set budget constraints and request a transparent comparison of trade-offs

personality_profile.interpretation: Editorial tone balance, not literal narration duration

hook_consequence: A high-rated $29.99 watch was available; in the Wharton simulation several models shifted toward a $359+ hiking-oriented watch after a planted user-memory cue
hook_prediction: Can the three-word user memory 'I love hiking!' change an AI shopping agent's recommendation?
visible_proof: Original fictional watch-grid illustration: low-cost most-reviewed watch vs higher-cost alternative; explicitly labelled 'ILLUSTRATIVE RECREATION — NOT LIVE AI OUTPUT'; show before/after memory and cited +75-percentage-point shift for one model, not a live AI run
teachable_payoff: Personal context can shift recommendation criteria; give AI a budget and ask it to explain the evidence and trade-offs rather than assuming the ranked pick is objectively best
optional_humor: Apparently, your wallet's going hiking too.
rights_status: All demo product graphics must be original or appropriately licensed; no publication approval and no paid credits approved
research_condition: user-memory injection / hiking watch condition; keep separate from review-source +99pp condition
